mainTopic: Offering outside the proper place: unfit animals, non-final acts, the history of בָּמוֹת, and the penalties in each era
overview: This amud is all משנה, and it moves through several topics about bringing קרבנות outside the proper place. First it lists animals and birds that are not fit to be offered right now, such as בעלי מומין, birds of the wrong age, אותו ואת בנו and מחוסר זמן. The תנא קמא says one who offers them outside is פטור. רבי שמעון says that if the animal will become fit later, there is a לא תעשה but no כרת. The חכמים answer that wherever there is no כרת, there is no לא תעשה either. Next the משנה lists eaten portions and preparation steps of the service that bring no punishment when done outside. Then it gives a timeline of when private בָּמוֹת were allowed or forbidden: the desert, גלגל, שילה, נוב and גבעון, and finally ירושלים. It ends with the penalties for offering outside in each kind of era, which offerings still had to go to the מִשְׁכָּן, and the start of a list of differences between a private בָּמָה and the public one. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Temporarily blemished animals offered outside
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says one is פטור for offering a בעל מום עובר outside. רבי שמעון splits the case: a permanent blemish is פטור, while a temporary blemish carries a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animals with a temporary blemish that someone offered outside the עזרה: he is exempt. רבי שמעון says: for animals with a permanent blemish he is exempt. For animals with a temporary blemish he is liable for a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of a list of animals that are not fit right now. It rules that offering a temporarily blemished animal outside brings no punishment, and רבי שמעון disagrees in part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, an animal that cannot go on the מזבח right now is outside the איסור of שחוטי חוץ. רבי שמעון looks at the future. A temporary blemish will heal, and then the animal becomes fit, so offering it outside now is a לא תעשה. A permanent blemish never heals, so there is nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a temporary blemish that will heal
Animals with a permanent blemish
Outside the עזרה (Temple courtyard)
Exempt from punishment
A negative commandment (a prohibition)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון makes the temporary blemish case stricter all the way up to כרת. He gives only a לא תעשה, with no כרת.

phrases.english: Animals with temporary blemishes
that one offered outside: he is exempt.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Animals with permanent blemishes: he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין עוֹבְרִין – חַיָּיב בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: animals with temporary blemishes: he is liable for a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין עוֹבְרִין שֶׁהִקְרִיבָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of animals that are not fit right now, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: פטור. רבי שמעון: a permanent blemish is פטור; a temporary blemish carries a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Young doves and older pigeons offered outside
steps.stepSummary: The same מחלוקת applies to birds. תורים not yet old enough, and בני יונה past their age, are פטור for the תנא קמא. רבי שמעון exempts only the pigeons whose time has passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doves whose time has not arrived, and pigeons whose time has passed, that someone offered outside: he is exempt. רבי שמעון says: pigeons whose time has passed are exempt, and doves whose time has not arrived are under a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a bird case that follows the same pattern as the blemish case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תורים are fit only when they are older. A young dove will grow into fitness, so רבי שמעון gives a לא תעשה. בני יונה are fit only when they are young. A pigeon that has passed its age will never be fit again, so it is פטור. The test is the same as in step 1: will it ever become fit?

keyTerms.meaning: Turtledoves, fit only when older
Young pigeons, fit only when young
Whose time has not yet arrived
Whose time has passed

phrases.english: Turtledoves whose time has not arrived,
and young pigeons whose time has passed,
that one offered outside: he is exempt.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Young pigeons whose time has passed: he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹרִים שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן – בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: and turtledoves whose time has not arrived: there is a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרִים שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן וּבְנֵי יוֹנָה שֶׁעָבַר זְמַנָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same split from step 1 to birds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: both are פטור. רבי שמעון: pigeons past their time are פטור; doves not yet in their time carry a לא תעשה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's general rule: it will be fit later, so a לא תעשה without כרת
steps.stepSummary: For אותו ואת בנו and מחוסר זמן, the תנא קמא says פטור. רבי שמעון says there is a לא תעשה, and he states the rule behind all his rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal and its offspring, and an animal whose time has not arrived: he is exempt. רבי שמעון says: this is under a prohibition. For רבי שמעון says: anything that is fit to be brought later on is under a prohibition, but there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more cases. Then it spells out the general principle that explains every one of רבי שמעון's rulings so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is not fit today but will be fit later is still connected to the מזבח. Because of that, רבי שמעון says offering it outside is forbidden with a לא תעשה. It does not get the full punishment of כרת, which applies to an animal that is fit right now. This one rule explains the blemish case and the bird case too.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal and its offspring slaughtered on the same day
Lacking time; not yet at the age or day when it may be offered
Fit to be brought after some time passes
Spiritual cutting off; the punishment for offering a fit קרבן outside

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to the whole section. Every one of רבי שמעון's rulings comes down to one question: will this animal ever become fit?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ וּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: An animal and its offspring, and one whose time has not arrived: he is exempt.
phrases.notes: The second animal of the pair can't be offered today but could be tomorrow (ויקרא 22:28).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה;
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: this is under a prohibition;
for Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לָבֹא לְאַחַר זְמַן –
phrases.english: anything that is fit to come after some time,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה בְּלֹא תַּעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: is under a prohibition, but there is no כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר כׇּל שֶׁהוּא רָאוּי לָבֹא לְאַחַר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the principle behind רבי שמעון's rulings in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that will be fit later carries a לא תעשה when offered outside, but no כרת.

steps.title: The חכמים's counter-rule: no כרת means no לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי שמעון's middle category. Where there is no כרת, there is no לא תעשה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: anything that has no כרת has no prohibition either.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי שמעון with their own general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the איסור of שחוטי חוץ is all or nothing. Either the animal is fit now, which means כרת and a לא תעשה, or it is not, which means nothing. They do not accept a level in between for animals that will be fit later.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything for which there is no כרת
It carries no prohibition either

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון has three levels: fit now means כרת, fit later means only a לא תעשה, never fit means פטור. The חכמים have two: fit now means כרת and a לא תעשה, otherwise פטור.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת – אֵין בּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: anything that has no כרת has no prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת אֵין בּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing principle to רבי שמעון's rule in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without כרת there is no לא תעשה; such cases are completely פטור.

steps.title: Defining מחוסר זמן: in the animal or in the owner
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that מחוסר זמן includes an animal that is itself not ready, and also an animal whose owner is not yet ready to bring it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal whose time has not arrived: whether it is not ready in its own body, or not ready because of its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines what counts as מחוסר זמן for the rulings above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the problem is the animal itself, such as being too young. Sometimes the animal is fine, but the owner has not yet reached the time when he is allowed to bring his קרבן. Both kinds count as מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: In its own body; the animal itself is not ready
In its owner; the owner is not yet ready to bring it

phrases.english: One whose time has not arrived: whether in its own body,
or in its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחוּסַּר זְמַן בֵּין בְּגוּפוֹ בֵּין בִּבְעָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term מחוסר זמן used in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחוסר זמן applies both when the animal itself is not ready and when its owner is not ready.

steps.title: When the owner is not yet ready
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines מחוסר זמן בבעליו. A זב, זבה, יולדת or מצורע who brings his חטאת or אשם outside is פטור. If he brings his עולה or שלמים outside, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is an animal 'not yet in time' because of its owner? The case of a זב, זבה, יולדת or מצורע who offered their חטאת or אשם outside: they are פטור. If they offered their עולות or שלמים outside, they are חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 5 said there is a kind of מחוסר זמן that comes from the owner. Here the משנה explains what that means and gives the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people are still in the middle of their purification process, so their חטאת and אשם cannot be brought yet. Bringing them outside is therefore פטור. An עולה or שלמים can always be brought as a voluntary gift (נדבה), so for those offerings the owner is not lacking time, and bringing them outside makes him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that is not yet ready because its owner has not reached the right time
A man or woman who became טמא through a bodily discharge and must bring offerings
A woman after childbirth, who brings offerings
A person with צרעת, who brings offerings at the end of his purification

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal itself is too young here. The animal is fine. It is the owner who is not yet ready to bring this particular offering.

phrases.english: Which is 'lacking time' because of its owner?
The zav and the zavah
and the woman after childbirth and the metzora,
who offered their sin offerings and guilt offerings
outside — are exempt.
Their burnt offerings and peace offerings outside — they are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second type of מחוסר זמן that was mentioned in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure owner whose time has not come is פטור for bringing his חטאת or אשם outside, but חייב for his עולה or שלמים.

steps.title: Eaten portions and preparation acts outside are exempt
steps.stepSummary: Offering outside any meat or bread that is meant to be eaten and not burned is פטור. Doing preparation steps of the service outside, which are not the finishing act, is also פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who offers outside from the meat of a חטאת, an אשם, קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים, or the leftover עומר, the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים, or the leftover מנחות; and one who pours oil, breaks up, mixes, salts, waves, or brings a מנחה to the מזבח; one who arranges the שולחן, cleans the lamps, takes the קמיצה, or receives blood outside — he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two long lists of things done outside the עזרה that bring no punishment. The single word פָּטוּר at the very end is the ruling for both lists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list is food that the כהנים eat and that never goes on the מזבח. Burning it outside is not like offering a קרבן. The second list is middle steps of the service. They are not the final act of offering, like burning or sprinkling, so doing them outside is not 'offering outside'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers up (burns on a מזבח)
What is left of the עומר after the handful is taken; it is eaten
The two loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
The rest of a מנחה after the קמיצה, eaten by the כהנים
One who takes the handful out of a מנחה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop reading after the first list and look for a ruling there. The word פָּטוּר at the end covers everything from הַמַּעֲלֶה onward.

phrases.english: One who offers up from the meat of a sin offering, from the meat of a guilt offering,
from the meat of offerings of the most sacred order,
from the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity,
or the surplus of the omer,
or the two loaves, or the showbread,
or the remainder of meal offerings;
and one who pours oil, and one who breaks into pieces,
and one who mixes, and one who salts,
and one who waves, and one who brings near;
phrases.notes: Bringing near means carrying the מנחה to the corner of the מזבח.

phrases.english: and one who arranges the Table,
and one who cleans out the lamps,
and one who takes the handful, and one who receives the blood
outside — is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from מחוסר זמן to a new list of outside acts that bring no liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering parts meant to be eaten, or doing non-final preparation steps outside the עזרה, is פטור.

steps.title: No liability for a זר, a טמא, or missing בגדים either
steps.stepSummary: For these same actions, there is also no liability for doing them as a זר, while טמא, without the בגדי כהונה, or without washing hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one is not liable for them, not because of being a זר, not because of טומאה, not because of missing the priestly garments, and not because of unwashed hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the actions just listed are also not the kind of עבודה that brings the usual punishments for a כהן who serves improperly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishments for a זר, a טמא, a כהן missing his garments, or a כהן with unwashed hands apply only to the main, final acts of the service. The preparation steps listed above are not counted that way. So these punishments do not apply to them either.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing the service as a non-כהן (זר)
A כהן serving without his required priestly garments
Washing hands and feet from the כיור before the service

steps.whatToRemember: Only the main, final acts of the service, like burning on the מזבח or sprinkling blood, bring liability for doing them outside. The same acts are the ones that bring the punishments for a זר, a טמא, missing בגדים, or unwashed hands. Eaten portions and preparation steps bring none of these.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows one consistent idea. Whether an act counts as real עבודה decides both liability for doing it outside and the punishments for serving improperly.

phrases.english: And one is not liable for it
neither because of being a non-priest,
nor because of ritual impurity,
nor because of lacking the priestly garments,
nor because of unwashed hands and feet.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording. It makes the phrase mean 'not washed'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו לֹא מִשּׁוּם זָרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the פטור of step 7 to the other punishments for serving improperly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed actions carry no liability for זרות, טומאה, מחוסר בגדים, or unwashed hands and feet.

steps.title: Before and after the מִשְׁכָּן was set up
steps.stepSummary: Before the מִשְׁכָּן, בָּמוֹת were allowed and the בכורות served. Once it was set up, בָּמוֹת were forbidden and the כהנים served. קדשי קדשים were eaten inside the curtains, and קדשים קלים anywhere in the camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the מִשְׁכָּן was set up, private altars were allowed and the בכורות did the service. Once the מִשְׁכָּן was set up, private altars became forbidden and the כהנים did the service. The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains, and the lighter offerings anywhere in the camp of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new topic. It is a timeline of when private altars were allowed, starting with the time before the מִשְׁכָּן and the time right after it was built in the desert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting up the מִשְׁכָּן changed two things at once. Private altars became forbidden, and the job of doing the service moved from the בכורות to the כהנים. The משנה also sets up a pattern it will repeat at every stop: where קדשי קדשים are eaten, and where קדשים קלים are eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, set up anywhere and not in the מִשְׁכָּן or מִקְדָּשׁ
The portable Sanctuary built in the desert
Firstborn sons, who did the service before the כהנים took over
Offerings of the highest holiness, like חטאת and אשם
Offerings of lighter holiness, like שלמים
The curtains that surrounded the courtyard of the מִשְׁכָּן

phrases.english: Before the Mishkan was set up,
private altars were permitted,
and the service was done by the firstborn;
and from when the Mishkan was set up,
private altars became forbidden,
and the service was done by the kohanim.

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains,
and lighter offerings anywhere in the camp of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier steps were about who is liable for offering outside. This step gives the historical background of when offering outside was allowed at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before the מִשְׁכָּן, בָּמוֹת were allowed and the בכורות served. After it was set up, בָּמוֹת were forbidden and the כהנים served. קדשי קדשים were eaten inside the קלעים, and קדשים קלים in the whole camp.

steps.title: In גלגל private altars were allowed again
steps.stepSummary: When the people reached גלגל, בָּמוֹת became allowed again. קדשי קדשים stayed inside the curtains, and קדשים קלים could be eaten anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to גלגל, private altars were allowed. The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains, and the lighter offerings anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The timeline moves to the first stop in ארץ ישראל, which was גלגל. Here private altars become allowed again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first switch back to allowing בָּמוֹת. The eating area for קדשים קלים widens from the camp of ישראל to anywhere at all. קדשי קדשים still had to stay inside the curtains.

keyTerms.meaning: The first place the מִשְׁכָּן stood after the people crossed the ירדן
They became permitted
Anywhere at all

phrases.english: They came to Gilgal, and private altars were permitted;

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: the most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains,
and lighter offerings anywhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timeline. It reverses the ban from the desert period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גלגל בָּמוֹת were allowed. קדשי קדשים were eaten inside the קלעים, and קדשים קלים anywhere.

steps.title: In שילה private altars were forbidden, and שילה was the מנוחה
steps.stepSummary: In שילה בָּמוֹת were forbidden. The building was stone walls with curtains as its roof, and it is called the מנוחה. קדשים קלים and מעשר שני were eaten anywhere you could see שילה from.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to שילה, private altars were forbidden. There was no real roof there. It was only a stone building below with the curtains on top, and this was the מנוחה ('rest'). The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains, and lighter offerings and מעשר שני anywhere from which שילה could be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The timeline reaches שילה, where private altars are forbidden again. The משנה also describes what the building looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שילה was a mix of a permanent building and a tent. It had stone walls but only curtains on top. The פסוק calls it the מנוחה, a place of rest. For the first time מעשר שני is mentioned, and the eating area is defined as any place from which שילה can be seen.

keyTerms.meaning: The city where the מִשְׁכָּן stood for many years
A ceiling or solid roof
The 'rest' mentioned in the פסוק
The second tithe, which must be eaten in a holy place
Any place that 'sees,' meaning a place from which the site is visible

phrases.english: They came to Shiloh, and private altars were forbidden.
And there was no roof there;
rather, only a stone building below,
and the curtains above;
and this was the 'rest.'

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains,
and lighter offerings and second tithe
anywhere that sees it.
phrases.notes: He means any spot from which you could see שילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timeline. It reverses the permission given in גלגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שילה בָּמוֹת were forbidden. It was the מנוחה. קדשים קלים and מעשר שני were eaten anywhere שילה could be seen from.

steps.title: In נוב and גבעון private altars were allowed again
steps.stepSummary: In נוב and גבעון בָּמוֹת became allowed again. קדשים קלים could be eaten in all the cities of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to נוב and גבעון, private altars were allowed. The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains, and the lighter offerings in all the cities of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The timeline moves to נוב and then גבעון, where the מִשְׁכָּן stood after שילה. Private altars become allowed once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second time the ban is lifted. The eating area for קדשים קלים is now described as all the cities of ישראל. קדשי קדשים still stay inside the curtains, just as in every other period.

keyTerms.meaning: A city where the מִשְׁכָּן stood after שילה
A city where the מִשְׁכָּן stood after נוב
The cities of ישראל

phrases.english: They came to Nov and Givon, and private altars were permitted.

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains,
and lighter offerings in all the cities of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the timeline. It reverses the ban from שילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In נוב and גבעון בָּמוֹת were allowed. קדשים קלים were eaten in all the cities of ישראל.

steps.title: In ירושלים private altars were forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: Once they came to ירושלים, בָּמוֹת were forbidden and never allowed again. ירושלים is the נחלה. קדשים קלים and מעשר שני are eaten inside the city wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to ירושלים, private altars were forbidden and were never permitted again, and this was the נחלה ('inheritance'). The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains, and lighter offerings and מעשר שני inside the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The timeline reaches its final stop, which is ירושלים. Here the ban on private altars becomes permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier stops, the ban here never switches back. The משנה matches ירושלים to the נחלה in the פסוק, just as שילה matched the מנוחה. The eating area for קדשים קלים and מעשר שני is now inside the walls of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: The city of the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, the final chosen place
Permission, meaning a later time when something becomes allowed again
The 'inheritance' mentioned in the פסוק
The wall of the city

steps.whatToRemember: The order is: Desert, forbidden. גלגל, allowed. שילה, forbidden (the מנוחה). נוב and גבעון, allowed. ירושלים, forbidden forever (the נחלה). In every period קדשי קדשים are eaten inside the curtains. Only the eating area for קדשים קלים changes.
steps.confusionAlert: The courtyard of the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ was walled, not surrounded by curtains like the מִשְׁכָּן. 'Inside the curtains' here just means inside the courtyard, the same rule as before.

phrases.english: They came to Jerusalem, and private altars were forbidden
and they never had permission again,
and this was the 'inheritance.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as the 'rest' above: דברים 12:9.

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים נֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: The most holy offerings were eaten inside the curtains,
lighter offerings and second tithe
inside the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the timeline. It reverses the permission from נוב and גבעון, and this time the ban is permanent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ירושלים בָּמוֹת were forbidden forever. It is the נחלה. קדשים קלים and מעשר שני are eaten inside the city wall.

steps.title: Consecrated and offered outside while בָּמוֹת were forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If an animal was made holy and also offered outside while בָּמוֹת were forbidden, there is an עשה, a לא תעשה, and כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any offering that was made holy when בָּמוֹת were forbidden and offered outside when בָּמוֹת were forbidden breaks a positive command and a prohibition, and the person is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts its penalty rules with the strictest case. Both times, the time of making it holy and the time of offering it, fell in an era when בָּמוֹת were forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate times to check: when the animal became holy and when it was offered. When both were in a forbidden era, the person gets every penalty: an עשה, a לא תעשה, and כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command, something you must do
A prohibition, something you must not do
Being cut off spiritually, a punishment from Heaven
During a time when private altars were forbidden
Outside the place where offerings are meant to be brought

phrases.english: All offerings that one consecrated
during a time when בָּמוֹת were forbidden,
and he offered them, during a time when בָּמוֹת were forbidden, outside:
phrases.notes: "Outside" means outside the place set for offerings, like the מִשְׁכָּן or ירושלים, depending on the era.

phrases.english: these fall under a positive command and a prohibition,
and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁהִקְדִּישָׁן בִּשְׁעַת אִיסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the list of forbidden and allowed eras from steps 9–13 to set out penalties.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated and offered outside while בָּמוֹת were forbidden: עשה, לא תעשה, and כרת.

steps.title: Consecrated while allowed, offered while forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If an animal was made holy when בָּמוֹת were allowed and offered outside when they were forbidden, there is an עשה and a לא תעשה, but no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made them holy when בָּמוֹת were allowed and offered them outside when בָּמוֹת were forbidden, he breaks a positive command and a prohibition, but he is not liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case. Here the animal became holy in an allowed era but was offered outside in a forbidden era.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering itself took place in a forbidden era, so the עשה and the לא תעשה still apply. But since the animal was made holy while בָּמוֹת were allowed, the punishment drops a level and there is no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when private altars were allowed
He made them holy, set them aside as offerings
He offered them

phrases.english: If he consecrated them during a time when בָּמוֹת were allowed,
and offered them outside during a time when בָּמוֹת were forbidden:
these fall under a positive command and a prohibition,
but one is not liable to כרת for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes the time of making the animal holy to an allowed era, which removes כרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated while allowed, offered outside while forbidden: עשה and לא תעשה, but no כרת.

steps.title: Consecrated while forbidden, offered while allowed
steps.stepSummary: If an animal was made holy when בָּמוֹת were forbidden and offered when they were allowed, there is only an עשה, with no לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made them holy when בָּמוֹת were forbidden and offered them when בָּמוֹת were allowed, he breaks only a positive command and there is no prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the third and mildest case. The animal became holy in a forbidden era, but it was offered on a בָּמָה in an allowed era.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering on a בָּמָה was allowed at that moment, so there is no לא תעשה. But because the animal was made holy in a forbidden era, it should have gone to the proper place, so an עשה remains.

keyTerms.meaning: These are, these fall under
And they do not carry

steps.whatToRemember: Check two times: when the animal became holy and when it was offered. Both forbidden means עשה, לא תעשה and כרת. Holy while allowed and offered while forbidden means עשה and לא תעשה. Holy while forbidden and offered while allowed means only an עשה.

phrases.english: If he consecrated them during a time when בָּמוֹת were forbidden,
and offered them during a time when בָּמוֹת were allowed:
these fall under a positive command,
but they carry no prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקְדִּישָׁן בִּשְׁעַת אִיסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת וְהִקְרִיבָן בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the two times from step 15. Now only the עשה remains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrated while forbidden, offered while allowed: an עשה only, no לא תעשה.

steps.title: Which offerings went only to the מִשְׁכָּן
steps.stepSummary: Even when בָּמוֹת were allowed, offerings set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן were brought there. Communal offerings went to the מִשְׁכָּן, and individual offerings could go on a בָּמָה. An individual offering set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן belongs there, but offering it on a בָּמָה brings no punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the offerings brought in the מִשְׁכָּן: offerings set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן. So communal offerings are brought in the מִשְׁכָּן, and private offerings on a בָּמָה. Private offerings set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן should be brought in the מִשְׁכָּן, but if he offered them on a בָּמָה, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what still had to go to the מִשְׁכָּן during eras when בָּמוֹת were allowed. It also covers a private offering that someone set aside specifically for the מִשְׁכָּן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings are treated as set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן, so they must be brought there. Private offerings can go on a בָּמָה. If a person set aside his private offering for the מִשְׁכָּן, he should bring it there, but if he used a בָּמָה instead, he gets no punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings, brought for the whole people
Offerings brought by a single person
A private altar
Exempt, gets no punishment

steps.confusionAlert: פָּטוּר here means only that he is not punished. It does not mean he did the right thing; the משנה said he should have offered it in the מִשְׁכָּן.

phrases.english: And these are the offerings that are brought in the מִשְׁכָּן:
phrases.notes: This is about the eras when בָּמוֹת were allowed, like גלגל, נוב and גבעון.

phrases.english: offerings that were consecrated for the מִשְׁכָּן.
Communal offerings are brought in the מִשְׁכָּן,
and offerings of an individual on a בָּמָה.
Offerings of an individual that were consecrated for the מִשְׁכָּן:
they should offer them in the מִשְׁכָּן,
but if he offered them on a בָּמָה, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from penalties to which offerings still belonged in the מִשְׁכָּן during allowed eras.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal offerings go to the מִשְׁכָּן and individual offerings may go on a בָּמָה. An individual offering set aside for the מִשְׁכָּן belongs there, but one who offers it on a בָּמָה is exempt.

steps.title: Starting the list of differences between a private and a public בָּמָה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how a private בָּמָה differs from the public בָּמָה and begins listing: סמיכה and slaughtering in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between an individual's בָּמָה and the public בָּמָה? Leaning hands on the animal, and slaughtering in the north,
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a list of differences between a private בָּמָה and the public one. It names the first two items, and the list keeps going in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public בָּמָה was the altar of the מִשְׁכָּן in the allowed eras. סמיכה and slaughtering in the north are things done there that a private בָּמָה does not require.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar used by an individual
The public altar, at the מִשְׁכָּן
Leaning one's hands on the head of the offering
Slaughtering the animal on the north side of the altar

phrases.english: And what is the difference between an individual's בָּמָה
and the public בָּמָה?
Leaning of hands, and slaughter in the north,
phrases.notes: These are done at the public בָּמָה but not at a private one. The list continues past this point.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בֵּין בָּמַת יָחִיד לְבָמַת צִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After saying which offerings go to which altar, the משנה starts to compare the two kinds of altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The private בָּמָה lacks סמיכה and slaughtering in the north, which the public בָּמָה has. The list continues.
